start.text: At the top of the stair, the wind finds a seam in every pane. The great lens stands dark. Beside the burner: a trimmed wick, a box of matches, and a tin with a little paraffin still in it.

choices.text: Check the lamp before lighting it.
Edith left it ready for someone.
Fill the burner and strike a match.

inspect.text: No cracked glass. No broken feed. A pale thumbprint marks the brass beneath the wick adjuster. Someone polished everything except the place they held on.

edith.text: You turn the matchbox over. The striking strip is worn almost smooth. You put it back exactly where she left it, then think better of that and take a match.

relight.text: The first match goes out. You cup the second in both hands. The wick catches; the flame settles. Beyond the glass, a narrow reach of water comes back into the world.

answer.text: Out past the north rocks, a light appears. Three flashes. Then dark. You count through the silence. It happens again.

choices.text: Look for the buoy that could be making it.
Watch for the rhythm Edith described.
Go down and tell Tom what you saw.
Stay beside the lamp and watch.

skeptic_view.text: You find the buoy when the beam comes round. Its light is steady. The other one is gone. You keep looking for a second buoy.

believer_view.text: Three flashes. You count them against the words in the ledger. On the next sweep, you lift a hand before you know why. Nothing in the glass moves but your reflection.

tom_view.text: You take one step toward the stair. From here the radio is only a floor below, but you rehearse the words as if Tom were very far away. A light. Three flashes. No, not the buoy.

watch.text: You draw the stool up beside the lens. The seat is cold through your clothes. You leave your hands in your lap and wait for the beam to come round.

end.text: The lamp turns. The north rocks disappear into fog again. You keep counting after there is nothing left to count.

quiet_view.text: You keep counting the flashes. If Tom asks, the lamp is working. That is all you need to tell him.
